key_insight: LowNet uses a looped, wavelet-inspired neural network with just 24 trainable scalars to solve Poisson equations.
engineering_relevance: Its compact parameterization and claimed linear computational complexity could support efficient Poisson solvers for simulation and image reconstruction.
method: Represent four independent 5×5 kernels with six parameters each.
Reuse the wavelet block through residual loops without adding trainable parameters.
Use wavelet transforms for linear computational complexity.
evidence_signal: On 10,000 images, the abstract reports PSNRs of 47.27, 74.14, and 100.74 dB for one, two, and three loops, respectively.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish generalization across boundary conditions, geometries, or engineering-scale problems; additional loops also require extra computation.
paper_title: LowNet: Looped Wavelet Neural Networks with 24 Learnable Parameters for Solving Poisson Equations
